analysis.title: SCIB Macro & Markets Chartbook - On Hold, but Not Done Hiking
key_insights: The FOMC, ECB and BoJ all left rates unchanged this week. All three were widely expected to hold, but markets price further tightening at each of their December meetings.

FOMC: the overall message was not hawkish. Chair Warsh wants to give as little forward guidance as possible, and the Fed will reduce the number of policy-setting meetings per year. His explanation for not hiking despite persistently high inflation was somewhat lacking.

The US front end rallied after the FOMC. The 2s10s UST curve bull steepened on a less hawkish message, persistently elevated long-term inflation expectations, a resilient economy (3Q26 GDP growth 3.4% SAAR) and safe-haven flows into government bonds.
Santander's US call is one final Fed hike in December, then a hold throughout 2027. That implies much less easing than the market currently prices.
ECB: rates were left unchanged with a clear hint at another hike in December, which is also Santander's base case. Santander expects the ECB to hike by less than the market expects.

ECB confidence factors: the statement says underlying inflation has remained broadly stable and wages show no material response, and it newly mentions tighter financing conditions likely weighing on inflation and growth. Oil prices are becoming less relevant for short-term ECB policy.
Market pricing suggests euro-area inflation may not return sustainably to the ECB's 2% target until at least mid-2028. Santander is watching next week's Eurozone inflation data.

ECB leadership: Lagarde will step down early on 7 February 2027 instead of 31 October 2027. Lane's term as chief economist ends in May 2027, and Schnabel has brought her departure forward to January 2027 from December. Governments will likely negotiate the three posts as a package.
Polymarket odds for the next ECB president: Pablo Hernández de Cos 34.5%, Klaas Knot 29%.

Brazil: Lula won the second round with 51.8% against 48.2% for Flavio Bolsonaro, against market expectations after the first round (45.2% vs 47%). 10y government bond yields rose about 230bp and the Ibovespa fell about 18% over the week, more than unwinding the post-first-round rally.

US earnings: with 288 S&P 500 companies (about 50% of index market cap) reported for 3Q26, the aggregate earnings surprise is 3%, the lowest in over eight quarters. The revenue surprise of 1.6% is the narrowest since 1Q25, and guidance upgrades are modest. Aggregate net income is up 25% YoY against an 11% 10-year average, but that has not met investor expectations.

US midterms are next Tuesday and Republicans are expected to lose their majority in Congress. Since 2006 every president entering the midterms with unified control of Congress has lost at least one chamber.

BoE: Santander firmly expects a 25bp hike next week, in line with 97% market pricing. It frames the move as risk management against inflation persistence, not the start of a sustained cycle, and expects the MPC to lean against the 84bp of further tightening priced for 2027.

UK peak overnight rate priced about 40bp above the US peak, a swing from 5bp lower at the start of the month. Santander expects the BoE to hold in December, while the market prices a 40% chance of back-to-back hikes.

UK Budget was good for gilts: the curve rallied about 5bp over Wednesday and Thursday. This year's issuance target rose £4.4bn and next year's financing need by £10bn, both less than Santander assumed. Average gross issuance over the next five months will be 24% lower than over the last seven, and two large redemptions in 1Q27 mean negative net issuance next quarter. The hard fiscal choices were left for next year.

tension_points.bull_case: Santander sees one final Fed hike in December and a hold through 2027, with the ECB hiking by less than the market expects, because underlying inflation is stable and tighter financing conditions weigh on growth.
tension_points.bear_case: Markets price further tightening at each December meeting and persistently elevated long-term inflation expectations and a resilient US economy (3.4% SAAR GDP) point to inflation persistence. The ECB outlook for returning to 2% remains challenging.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Euro-area inflation data due next week and any sign of wage second-round effects would challenge the ECB call.

tension_points.bull_case: A 25bp hike is a one-off risk-management move, and the MPC should lean against the 84bp of further tightening priced for 2027 and hold in December.
tension_points.bear_case: The market prices a 40% chance of back-to-back hikes, and the very high priced peak has become entrenched.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A BoE December hike, or MPC messaging that does not push back on the 2027 pricing, would invalidate the one-off framing.

theme_stances.key_argument: Santander expects one final Fed hike in December followed by a hold through 2027, and an ECB hike smaller than the market expects.

theme_stances.evidence: A hike to douse the spark, not extinguish a fire

theme_stances.key_argument: Issuance increases were smaller than assumed, gross issuance slows and net issuance turns negative next quarter.
theme_stances.evidence: good news for gilts, as the tough fiscal work is left for the future
